She wiggles the bottoms into place with a grin and immediately challenges him: “Your turn, slowcoach. Get that shirt off and let’s get in the water.” 

Benjamin hesitates — classic overthinking, anxiety about changing in public even though the nearest people are far away. Scarlett reads it perfectly: she turns her back to give him a sliver of privacy while teasing him (“you big baby”), then yanks his sock off when he asks for help, reaches in and pulls his shirt over his head in one smooth motion. The moment he is down to trunks she steps back, looks him up and down with a smirk, and the tension breaks into forward motion. They walk barefoot across the grass, hand in hand. 

The water is shockingly cold. Benjamin’s body reacts; he jokes about “a bad hair day” down there. Scarlett meets the self-deprecation with immediate warmth and zero judgment: “Trust me, I’ve seen you in every state possible. Cold water shrinkage is nothing new… I still think you look cute.” The first major beat of the day lands here — not erotic spectacle, but the lived experience of being known completely and still desired. He feels safe enough to name his shrinking without shame because she already knows every inch of him.
